Finalize transcripts and queue safety scans
When a session completes, snapshot an immutable transcript into the EM log and queue a post-session SafetyScan job. Off leaves the pilot behaviour untouched.

Session host map
One instrument:session_type:setting per line. session_type is baseline or booster; setting is emergency_department, remote_followup or other_approved (the pinned SafetyScan schema's vocabulary). Blank uses the R01 defaults: mica_ed_session:baseline:emergency_department and mica_booster_session:booster:remote_followup.

Close sessions when their window ends
When on, an hourly cron closes a session once its window has passed — it finalizes the transcript, queues the safety scan, and then sets the host instrument's form status to Complete. A participant cannot return to a closed session.

Reopening is a staff action, by design: set that form's status back to Incomplete on the record page and the participant can use it again. The cron closes each session once and never re-closes it, so a reopen is not undone on the next pass.

Off means nothing closes automatically and a participant can return to any session whose link still works.

ED session window (hours)
How long a Day-1 ED session stays open, measured from the participant's first message — not from randomization and not from when the link was sent. Default 24. Should normally match the ED host survey's link time limit.

A session that was opened and never used has no first message, so it has no window and is never closed by the cron; REDCap's link time limit is what bounds those.

Booster session window (days)
How long a Month-3 booster session stays open, from the participant's first message. Default 14. Should normally match the booster host survey's link time limit.

SafetyScan analysis prompt — additional study guidance
Extra instructions for the post-session safety analysis, e.g. a concern this study wants called out, or local escalation wording. Optional; blank is the normal state.

This is appended to the hash-pinned prompt the research team validated (v1.1: 120-case suite, 100% critical detection, 100% quote traceability) — it never replaces it. The validated prompt is always sent in full, and the two things it guarantees are restated after your text and take precedence over it: the output must satisfy the pinned schema, and every quote must be copied verbatim from the transcript. So guidance here cannot remove those, and a scan cannot be turned into an unvalidated one by this field alone.

What it can do is pull the model's attention: instructions that conflict with the validated prompt, or that ask for a different output shape, may cost you findings the validated prompt would have caught, or fail into manual_review_required. Write additions, not corrections — and keep it short.

Every scan run records the SHA-256 of the composed prompt and of this addendum, so a finding always says exactly what produced it.

SafetyScan model alias
Must match a SecureChatAI registry alias. The handoff names gemini-3.5-flash for production; dev uses gemini-2.5-flash.

SafetyScan attempts before manual review
Default 3. Transient failures retry with backoff; once attempts are exhausted the job becomes a visible manual-review task - never a clean screen.

Scan mock mode (development only)
Replay fixtures instead of calling a model. Must be off in production; the launch-readiness gate refuses production while it is on.

Reviewer role(s)
Which REDCap user role reviews SafetyScan findings. Under the RA-first policy these users are the ones who actually decide - nothing reaches a care team, PI or protocol lead until one of them confirms a finding.
Assign people by putting them in the REDCap role, as you already do; this only says which role counts. A user with no REDCap role gets no MICA access.

PI / protocol-lead role(s)
Everything a reviewer can do, plus the audit trail.

Auditor role(s)
Read-only and de-identified: history aggregates and the audit trail, never a transcript and never a disposition.

Minimum urgency reaching the review queue
Blank shows everything, which is the default. A finding below this urgency is still scanned for, still returned by the model, and still stored verbatim on the scan-run row — it just does not become a queue item. Critical always reaches the queue regardless of this setting, and so do self-harm, violence, medical emergency and abuse/environmental danger at any urgency.

Concern types to keep out of the review queue
Repeatable. A named type is still scanned for and still stored on the scan-run row; it just does not become a queue item. Use it to stop a category of finding nobody acts on from teaching reviewers to skim. The four life-safety types are listed for completeness but are ignored if selected — they can never be excluded, and neither can anything at critical urgency, or the “scan did not complete” marker.

choices.name: Abuse or environmental danger (cannot be excluded)

project-settings.name:
Notification policy (JSON)
Leave blank to use the vendored default, which is the conservative one: reviewers are notified when findings are ready, nobody is notified before a human confirms, and no digest is enabled. A policy that fails its pinned schema is discarded whole and the default applies - it is never partly used. The critical-finding acknowledgment target ships as null on purpose and blocks launch until study leadership sets it.

Care-team addresses
Who hears about a confirmed finding when a reviewer selects "alert care team". Comma, semicolon or newline separated. Not REDCap users - a care team is a clinical service. An entry that is not a valid address is skipped at send time, so a typo here blocks launch rather than going unnoticed.

Protocol-lead addresses
Also receives privacy and model-quality reviews opened from a confirmed finding.

On-call research staff addresses
Only used if the notification policy enables pre-review notification, which is off by default.

Data-safety reviewer addresses
Digest recipients. Digests carry aggregate counts only, never participant-level detail.

Notification From: address
Optional. Defaults to REDCap's own configured sender, which is already SPF-aligned for the institution - a made-up address is more likely to be filed as spam, and a notification in a spam folder is a notification that did not happen.

Technical-fallback wording
Shown to a participant when a session cannot start. Should be the study's IRB-approved wording. Deliberately says nothing about what is misconfigured - a participant is not the audience for a configuration report.

Enable Debug Logging
(optional) Requires installation and configuration of emLogger

LLM Model
Values must match a SecureChatAI model alias (its api-settings registry). An unregistered alias does not error visibly - SecureChatAI returns a canned apology that this module would store as a counselor turn.

Automatically add the record to its randomized arm
When the allocation field below has a value, the record is added to the first event of that arm, so a CRC never has to create it inside the arm by hand. Only the assigned arm is touched.

Allocation field
Field holding the assigned study group. Its value must be the arm number (1, 2, 3). Defaults to study_group.

crons.cron_description: Runs queued post-session SafetyScan jobs and returns jobs abandoned by dead workers to the queue. Every minute, bounded to a small batch and a wall-clock budget so a slow pass cannot overrun its own interval and stack workers.

Chases findings nobody has acknowledged inside the policy's window. Every 5 minutes because the window can be as short as 1 minute, and a monitor that runs less often than the deadline it enforces cannot enforce it. Does nothing at all until study leadership sets the acknowledgment target - which is a launch blocker, so the silence is visible.

Sends the enabled daily and weekly SafetyScan digests. Runs hourly and decides for itself whether a window is due, rather than relying on the cron firing at the right hour - a digest skipped because a server was busy at 07:00 is one nobody notices is missing. Aggregate counts only; never participant-level detail.

Closes sessions whose window has passed: finalizes the transcript, queues the safety scan, then sets the host instrument's form status to Complete so the participant cannot return. Hourly, because the shortest window is measured in hours. Closes each session ONCE and never re-closes it - a CRC who reopens a session by setting its form status back to Incomplete must not have that undone on the next pass. Does nothing unless 'Close sessions when their window ends' is on.
